bugs.text: game.player is created without a y coordinate and it is never set (only updateCapture writes p.y). The ship is drawn at NaN (invisible in every play screenshot), player bullets have y=NaN so they never hit anything, collisions with enemies and enemy bullets never trigger, and the tractor beam can never catch the player. Score stays 0, the player cannot die, and stage 1 never ends: the game is unplayable.
Because bullet y is NaN, the off-screen removal b.y<-10 never fires; the two NaN bullets stay in game.bullets forever and the 2-shot limit blocks all further firing for the rest of the stage.
enemyFire uses the undefined player.y: vy becomes NaN and vx = dx*2.4, so enemy bullets shoot off sideways and are deleted immediately; enemies effectively never fire.
Hits are counted twice for every kill (once in the collision loop, once in killEnemy), so the results ratio is wrong and can exceed 100%.
Challenging-stage hits score 50/80/150 instead of 100 because entering enemies count as in formation; challenge bosses need two hits.
Enemy-hit sound sHit is defined but never called.
Breathing scale snaps back to 1 whenever any enemy leaves formation, making the formation jump.
Title score table has a stray '400 800 1600' row and a hint line wider than the canvas; '/' is not in the font, so it renders clipped with gaps.
Stage badge shows only one flag of the largest denomination instead of composing badges.
After one half of the dual fighter is lost, the remaining ship stays at the centre instead of the surviving half's position.

summary: The file is tidy and well organised: a correct fixed-timestep loop, crisp integer scaling, a good starfield, a full 40-enemy formation that flies in on looping paths, sways and breathes, Boss dives with Goei escorts, and code for the tractor beam, capture, rescue, dual fighter, challenging stages and synthesized sounds. But one missing field, the player's y coordinate, which is never initialised, quietly breaks almost everything. The ship is invisible, its two shots become NaN and never hit or expire, enemy bullets fly off sideways, and no collision can ever happen. The play-test confirms this: score 0 after 90 s, no ship on screen, the same stage-1 formation forever, and alive_at_end only because the player is invulnerable. Most of the Galaga mechanics exist only as unreachable code, so as delivered the game cannot be played.
